hints: Factor the top and the bottom: (x + 5)(x − 3) over (x − 9)(x + 2).
Mark −5, −2, 3 and 9 on a number line. The sign flips each time you cross one of them. Start from the right, where everything is positive.
1.why:
f = (x + 5)(x − 3)/((x − 9)(x + 2)). Right of 9: positive. Between 3 and 9: negative. Between −2 and 3: positive. Between −5 and −2: negative. Left of −5: positive.

So f < 0 exactly when −5 < x < −2 or 3 < x < 9. The other options pick the positive stretches.

hints: |n − a| < |n − b| means n is closer to a than to b, so it's on a's side of their midpoint.
Closer to 60 than 100 means n < 80. Closer to 100 than 20 means n > 60.
2.why:
Both conditions together: 60 < n < 80.

That's n = 61 to 79, which is 19 integers. 21 and 20 count one or both ends wrongly.

hints: Let the small box weigh w and cost p. The large box costs 2p and weighs W.
The large box's price per gram is 0.88 times the small box's: 2p/W = 0.88 × p/w.
3.why:
W/w = 2/0.88 = 2.2727.

So the large box is about 127.3% heavier. Nearest is 127.

hints: Turn every term into log(1 + x) and log(1 − x): log√y = ½ log y, and log(1/√(1 − x<sup>2</sup>)) = −½ log(1 − x) − ½ log(1 + x).
The log(1 + x) terms cancel. Solve for log(1 − x).
Set the first two baskets equal to find the price of an apple in mangoes.
Then set the second and third equal to find an orange in mangoes. Price any basket in mangoes.
5.why:
2a + 4o + 6m = a + 4o + 8m gives a = 2m. a + 4o + 8m = 8o + 7m gives 4o = a + m = 3m.

Basket 2 = 2m + 3m + 8m = 13 mangoes.

hints: Equilateral triangle area = (√3/4)s<sup>2</sup>. A regular hexagon is six of those triangles.
6.why:
6a2 = 144, so a2 = 24.

a = 2√6. 4√6 is the trap from forgetting to take the square root of 6 properly.

hints: Average price per kg = total money spent ÷ total kg bought, not the average of the five prices.
Pick a handy amount, like ₹100 for each of the first three months, and ₹50 for each of the last two.
7.why:
Kg bought: 100/10 + 100/20 + 100/25 + 50/25 + 50/50 = 10 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 22 kg.

Money spent: 400. 400/22 ≈ 18.2, so 18. 26 is the trap: that's the plain average of the five prices.

hints: Complete the square: x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 13 = (x − 2)<sup>2</sup> − 17.
Taking the absolute value flips the part below the axis. The flipped vertex sits at height 17. A flat line hits the graph 3 times only at one height.
8.why:
Below 17, the line y = r cuts the W shape 4 times. Above 17, only twice.

At r = 17 it touches the flipped vertex and cuts the two outer arms: 3 roots. So r = 17.

hints: Let him buy N pens and pay a wage w. Write profit as revenue − 8N − w for each case.
The two cases differ only in the price of the last N − 100 pens (₹11 vs ₹9), and the profit differs by ₹600.
Each year's interest is the previous year's interest times (1 + r).
Let v cc be taken out of bottle 1 and replaced from bottle 2. Bottle 1 still holds 800 cc.
Indigo balance: 33(800 − v) + 17v = 21 × 800.
11.why:
26400 − 16v = 16800, so v = 600 cc.

Bottle 2 gave away 600 of its 800 cc, so 200 cc is left.

hints: Use rates per month: Amar + Akbar = 1/12, Akbar + Anthony = 1/16, Anthony + Amar = 1/24.
Add all three to get twice the total rate. Then subtract each pair to get each person.
12.why:
Sum = 9/48, so all three together = 3/32 a month.

Amar = 3/32 − 1/16 = 1/32. Akbar = 3/32 − 1/24 = 5/96. Anthony = 3/32 − 1/12 = 1/96.

Akbar is fastest and Anthony slowest. Amar, in the middle, takes 32 months.

hints: 3 and 5 are always in, so you're choosing extras from {1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8}. You need at least one extra.
Count all subsets of those 6, take away the ones with both 7 and 8, then take away the empty one.
13.why:
All subsets: 26 = 64. With both 7 and 8: 24 = 16. That leaves 48.

Remove the empty set (the group would be just {3, 5}, only two numbers): 47.

hints: In a right triangle, inradius = (leg + leg − hypotenuse)/2. Here the inradius is 4.
With legs 10 and b, the hypotenuse is b + 2. Use Pythagoras.
In a regular hexagon, AD is a diameter of the circumcircle. So angle ACD is 90°.
AC = 2√3 for side 2, and CT = 1. Use Pythagoras in triangle ACT.
Let A admit a patients and B admit a + 21. Then 200/a = 152/(a + 21) + 3.
Clear the fractions, or try the TITA-friendly values that divide 200 nicely.
Write N + G = 6S and S + N = 2G.
From the second, N = 2G − S. Put that into the first to get G in terms of S, then N.
17.why:
3G − S = 6S gives G = 7S/3. Then N = 14S/3 − S = 11S/3.

Neeta earns most and Sita least: 11/3 : 1 = 11 : 3. 7 : 3 is the trap: that's Geeta to Sita.

hints: Group k has 2k − 1 numbers and ends at k<sup>2</sup>.
Group 15 runs from 14<sup>2</sup> + 1 to 15<sup>2</sup>.
Call the work 60 units. Anu does 4 a day, Vinu 5 and Manu 3.
Odd days are Vinu + Anu, even days are Vinu + Manu. Add up a two-day block.
19.why:
Odd day: 9 units. Even day: 8 units. Two days: 17.

After 6 days: 51 units. Day 7 adds 9, reaching 60. So 7 days. 6 is the trap: work isn't finished after 6.

hints: Write the number as abc. Reversed minus original = 99(c − a).
99(c − a) = 198 means c = a + 2. Count the choices for a and b.
20.why:
a can be 1 to 7 (so c ≤ 9), and b can be anything from 0 to 9.

7 × 10 = 70.

hints: The faster train passes a post in 12 s, so its speed is 160/12 m/s. Convert to km/h.
Opposite directions: add the speeds. In 14 s they cover both lengths together.
21.why:
Faster: 40/3 m/s = 48 km/h. Slower: 42 km/h = 35/3 m/s. Together: 25 m/s.

14 × 25 = 350 m = 160 + L, so L = 190 m.

hints: Work out the first several terms. The sequence repeats.
Find how long the cycle is, then reduce 2021 by it.
22.why:
x0 to x6: 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2. So it repeats every 5 terms.

2021 leaves 1 when divided by 5, so x2021 = x1 = 2.
